subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What happens to particles when a substance boils?
options: They gain energy and spread far apart as a gas
questions.explain: Boiling gives particles enough energy to overcome forces and move freely apart as a gas.

questions.q: In the particle model, what is true of particles in a gas?
options: Far apart and moving quickly in all directions
Touching but able to move past each other
questions.explain: Gas particles are far apart and move randomly at high speed.

questions.q: What did the alpha-particle scattering experiment suggest about the nucleus?
options: It is large and spread out
It is small, dense and positively charged
questions.explain: Most alpha particles passed through, but a few were deflected, showing a small dense positive nucleus.

questions.q: John Dalton's early model described atoms as:
options: Balls of positive charge with embedded electrons
Mostly empty space around a nucleus
Tiny solid spheres that cannot be divided
questions.explain: Dalton pictured atoms as tiny indivisible solid spheres.

questions.q: What is the relative formula mass (Mr) of water, H2O? (Ar: H=1, O=16)
In which state are particles most closely packed and only able to vibrate in fixed positions?
questions.explain: In a solid, particles are tightly packed in a regular arrangement and only vibrate.

questions.q: Copper ions produce which colour in a flame test?
questions.explain: Copper ions give a green flame colour.

questions.q: What is the electronic structure of a neutral chlorine atom (17 electrons)?
questions.explain: Filling shells 2 then 8 then 7 gives 2,8,7 for 17 electrons.

questions.q: Which scientist proposed that electrons orbit the nucleus in fixed energy shells?
questions.explain: Bohr suggested electrons occupy fixed shells (energy levels) around the nucleus.

questions.q: In a closed system, the total mass of the products of a reaction is:
questions.explain: Mass is conserved, so the products have the same total mass as the reactants.

questions.q: How is the mass number of an atom calculated?
questions.explain: Mass number is the total number of protons and neutrons.

questions.q: How many moles are in 80 g of NaOH? (Mr = 40)
questions.explain: moles = mass/Mr = 80/40 = 2 mol.

questions.q: Adding sodium hydroxide to iron(III) ions produces a precipitate that is:
questions.explain: Iron(III) ions give a brown precipitate of iron(III) hydroxide.

questions.q: A compound contains 0.3 mol of nitrogen and 0.9 mol of hydrogen. What is its empirical formula?
questions.explain: The ratio 0.3:0.9 simplifies to 1:3, giving NH3.

questions.q: Flame emission spectroscopy works by measuring the:
options: Light given out when metal ions are heated in a flame
questions.explain: In flame emission spectroscopy, heated metal ions emit light with a pattern that identifies them.

questions.q: Graphene is best described as:
options: A single layer of carbon atoms arranged in hexagons
A simple molecule of two carbons
questions.explain: Graphene is a single layer of graphite, one atom thick, in a hexagonal arrangement.

questions.q: Approximately how many particles are in one mole of a substance (Avogadro's constant)?
questions.explain: One mole contains 6.02×10^23 particles (Avogadro's constant).

questions.q: A solution has a concentration of 25 g/dm3. What mass of solute is in 2 dm3?
questions.explain: mass = concentration x volume = 25 x 2 = 50 g.

questions.q: What is the formula of the compound formed from Mg²⁺ and Cl⁻ ions?
questions.explain: Two Cl⁻ ions balance one Mg²⁺ ion, giving MgCl2.

questions.q: What is the approximate radius of an atom?
questions.explain: Atoms have a radius of about 1x10^-10 m, roughly 10,000 times larger than the nucleus.

questions.q: In ionic bonding, electrons are:
questions.explain: Electrons are transferred from the metal atom to the non-metal atom, forming ions.

questions.q: Which of these is a compound?
options: A mixture of salt and sand
questions.explain: Water is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen chemically bonded together.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry (4CH1) specification; Principles Of Chemistry
